title: Know Yourself Kindly
subtitle: Where your lens came from, who you are now, and who you are becoming
author: Christian
description_html:
Before you can share a life well, it helps to understand your own.

This short, warm book starts with you. Where did your way of seeing things come from: the home you grew up in, the old rules, the things life taught you? How are you wired today: your energy, your weather, the words that land and the ones that sting? And who are you becoming, one small step at a time?

Along the way it explains, in plain words, how feelings work, why your worth is not a score, why personality is more like a set of dials than a box, and how minds work differently, from ADHD and autism to sensory and learning differences.

Inside this book

  • Where your lens came from, and the rulebook from home
  • Your wiring, your weather and your words
  • Who you are becoming: one small goal and a kind monthly look at yourself
  • How feelings work, and naming what you feel
  • Self-worth, shame and a kinder inner voice
  • Personality and temperament: dials, not boxes
  • Minds that work differently, and meeting in the middle

Each chapter has everyday scenes (all made up), words you could use and one small thing to try this week. Three friendly characters, Professor Puddles, Tidbit and Sugarfoot, drop in with hints, and keep to the lighter pages. Where a chapter touches hard things, it says where to find help.

Part of a series. Spread Love & Acceptance is a series of short books that each stand on their own, plus a workbook with every form. Read them in any order.

Every chapter is also free to read online, in a short and a full version, with no account. The print and Kindle editions are for readers who prefer a book in hand. This book is general education, not therapy or a diagnosis.

title: Heal and Steady
subtitle: Stress, anger, worry, loss and repair, and finding your footing again
author: Christian
description_html:
Some days are heavy. This book helps you find your footing again, gently and without blame.

Stress piles up, anger flares, worry keeps you awake, or a loss changes everything. This book explains what is going on inside you, in plain words, and gives you small, practical things to try.

It explains what stress does to the body and why it adds up, what anger is for and what helps in the hot minutes, how worry, low mood and trauma work, and when and where to get help. It walks with you through grief in its many forms, through repair and apologies that land, and through the slow work of change. It ends with what matters to you, and what a good life can mean.

title: Understanding Each Other
subtitle: How we hear, see and belong to each other, at home and in every group
author: Christian
description_html:
Two people can care about each other and still fall out of tune.

One wants to talk now; the other needs an hour. A comment meant lightly lands hard. This book is about understanding the people around you: at home, in families, with friends, at work and in every group you belong to.

It explains how pace and tone pull people apart, how communication really works, and why two people can see the same moment so differently. It looks at why we need to belong, how trust grows and is rebuilt, how love takes many forms, and the quiet pull of groups. It ends with helping others well, with kind limits and without burning out.

Inside this book

  • Why we get out of tune, and how to get back
  • How communication works: meaning, listening and repair
  • How we see each other: perception, bias and the stories we tell
  • Attachment, trust and belonging
  • Closeness and love in many forms
  • Groups, influence and disagreeing kindly

title: Share the Load
subtitle: The work nobody sees, and a fair, kind way to share it
author: Christian
description_html:
Every shared home runs on work that nobody sees.

Noticing the shoes are too small, booking the appointment, remembering bin day: when that work is not counted, someone ends up carrying more than anyone realises, and resentment grows quietly.

This book helps you see the whole load, kindly and without keeping score. It shows a simple way to check whether the way you share the work can last, how much of a reaction is leftover stress, how to agree what fair means to each of you, and a gentle monthly look-back that catches what weekly chats miss. It works for couples, families, housemates, co-parents and teams. It looks at the setup, never at the person.

Inside this book

  • The work nobody sees: the mental load, made visible
  • Is the split working? A simple check you can both trust
  • Full stress tanks and seven angles on the same moment
  • Two kinds of fair, and letting words land
  • The monthly look-back
  • How the numbers work, in plain arithmetic
  • An afterword that draws the series together

title: The Workpapers: Free Forms, All in One
subtitle: Every workpaper from the series, on big pages, to fill in by hand
author: Christian
description_html:
Every workpaper from the series, on big pages with room to write.

Inside are blank copies of all ten: a quick check of how much you are carrying, a calm-down kit you make on a calm day, a self-check before you reply to something that stung, a 90-second daily check-in, a one-week log of who did what, a list that gives every job one owner, a monthly look-back, and more.

Each one starts with a short page that says when to use it, how long it takes, who fills it in and which book explains it. Then come spare copies for the weeks ahead, a planner for the six-week program and pages for your own notes. The same forms are free to print or fill in online; this book simply puts them all in one place.

Inside

  • 10 workpapers, 47 blank copies in all
  • A short guide page before each one
  • Single sheets on one page; longer sheets open across two facing pages
  • A six-week planner and lined pages for notes
  • Large 8.5 × 11 in pages

The sheets describe what happened, never who someone is. Fill them in on your own or together; on shared sheets each person writes only their own rows.
